# fastText

[fastText](https://fasttext.cc/) is a library for efficient learning of word representations and sentence classification.

## What is fastText?

fastText is a library for efficient text classification and representation learning. It can be used for:

- **Word representation learning**: Learn vector representations of words (word embeddings)
- **Text classification**: Classify text documents into categories (e.g., spam detection, sentiment analysis)
- **Language identification**: Detect the language of text

## Usage

fastText provides a command-line tool with the following main commands:

### Word Representation Learning

Train word vectors using the skipgram model:
```bash
$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model
```

Train word vectors using the cbow model:
```bash
$ ./fasttext cbow -input data.txt -output model
```

### Getting Word Vectors

Print word vectors for words in a file:
```bash
$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin < queries.txt
```

Get word vectors for out-of-vocabulary words using subword information:
```bash
$ ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
```

### Text Classification

Train a text classifier:
```bash
$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model
```

Test the classifier:
```bash
$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt
```

Predict labels for new text:
```bash
$ ./fasttext predict model.bin test.txt
```

Predict labels with probabilities:
```bash
$ ./fasttext predict-prob model.bin test.txt
```

### Quantization

Reduce model size with quantization:
```bash
$ ./fasttext quantize -output model
```

This creates a `.ftz` file with reduced memory footprint while maintaining functionality.

## Input Format

### For Supervised Learning (Text Classification)

Training data should be in a text file with one sample per line. Each line should contain labels prefixed with `__label__` followed by the text:

```
__label__positive This movie was great!
__label__negative Terrible experience.
__label__neutral It was okay.
```

### For Unsupervised Learning (Word Vectors)

Training data should be a text file with one sentence per line:

```
This is a sample sentence.
Here is another sentence for training.
Word vectors will be learned from this text.
```

## Command-Line Options

Common options include:

**Dictionary options:**
- `-minCount`: Minimal number of word occurrences (default: 5 for word vectors, 1 for classification)
- `-wordNgrams`: Max length of word n-grams (default: 1)
- `-minn`: Min length of character n-gram (default: 0)
- `-maxn`: Max length of character n-gram (default: 0)
- `-bucket`: Number of buckets (default: 2000000)

**Training options:**
- `-lr`: Learning rate (default: 0.1 for supervised, 0.05 for word vectors)
- `-dim`: Size of word vectors (default: 100)
- `-ws`: Size of context window (default: 5)
- `-epoch`: Number of epochs (default: 5 for supervised, 5 for word vectors)
- `-neg`: Number of negatives sampled (default: 5)
- `-loss`: Loss function - ns (negative sampling), hs (hierarchical softmax), or softmax (default: softmax for supervised, ns for word vectors)
- `-thread`: Number of threads (default: 12)

**Quantization options:**
- `-cutoff`: Number of words and n-grams to retain (default: 0)
- `-retrain`: Whether to fine-tune embeddings if cutoff is applied (default: 0)
- `-qnorm`: Whether to quantize the norm separately (default: 0)
- `-qout`: Whether to quantize the classifier (default: 0)
- `-dsub`: Size of each sub-vector (default: 2)

Run any command without arguments to see its full option list:
```bash
$ ./fasttext supervised
$ ./fasttext skipgram
$ ./fasttext cbow
```

## Pre-trained Models

fastText provides pre-trained models:
- Word vectors for 157 languages trained on Wikipedia and Common Crawl
- English word vectors
- Language identification models
- Various supervised task models

Visit [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/) for downloads and more information.

## Output Files

After training, fastText creates several files:

- `model.bin`: Full model file (can be used for further training or getting word vectors)
- `model.vec`: Text file containing word vectors (one per line)
- `model.ftz`: Quantized model file (smaller, load-only)

## Examples

### Example 1: Train Word Vectors

```bash
# Train skipgram model on text file
$ ./fasttext skipgram -input data.txt -output model -dim 300 -epoch 5

# Get vectors for specific words
$ echo "king queen man woman" | ./fasttext print-word-vectors model.bin
```

### Example 2: Text Classification

```bash
# Train classifier on labeled data
$ ./fasttext supervised -input train.txt -output model -epoch 25 -lr 1.0

# Test the model
$ ./fasttext test model.bin test.txt

# Predict on new data
$ ./fasttext predict model.bin -
> This is a test sentence
```

### Example 3: Quantization

```bash
# Quantize a model to reduce size
$ ./fasttext quantize -input model.bin -output model

# Use the quantized model (same as regular model)
$ ./fasttext test model.ftz test.txt
```

## Resources

- Website: [https://fasttext.cc/](https://fasttext.cc/)
- Documentation: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/](https://fasttext.cc/docs/)
- Pre-trained models: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/pretrained-vectors.html)
- Language identification: [https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html](https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/language-identification.html)

- Facebook group: https://www.facebook.com/groups/1174547215919768

"""Black-box regression tests for the command-line implementation.

Run after ./compile.sh with: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
An alternate development build can be selected using FASTTEXT_BIN.
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path
import struct
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
BINARY = os.environ.get("FASTTEXT_BIN", str(ROOT / "executable"))


class CommandLineTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.work = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.directory = Path(self.work.name)
        self.corpus = self.directory / "train.txt"
        self.corpus.write_text("__label__a x\n__label__b y\n")
        self.model = self.directory / "model"

    def tearDown(self):
        self.work.cleanup()

    def run_cli(self, *args, text=None):
        return subprocess.run(
            [BINARY, *map(str, args)], input=text, capture_output=True,
            text=True, timeout=20, cwd=self.directory,
        )

    def train(self, *options, command="supervised"):
        result = self.run_cli(
            command, "-input", self.corpus, "-output", self.model,
            "-dim", 2, "-thread", 1, "-wordNgrams", 2, "-bucket", 100,
            "-verbose", 0, *options,
        )
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, "")
        return self.model.with_suffix(".bin")

    def test_general_usage(self):
        result = self.run_cli()
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith("usage: fasttext <command> <args>\n\n"))
        self.assertIn("print-sentence-vectors", result.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.endswith("\n\n"))
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("not-a-command").stderr, result.stderr)

    def test_option_errors_and_contextual_help(self):
        result = self.run_cli("supervised", "-dim", 7, "-h")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith("Here is the help! Usage:\n\n"))
        self.assertIn("size of word vectors [7]", result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("[softmax]", result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("[ns]", self.run_cli("skipgram", "-h").stderr)
        self.assertTrue(self.run_cli("supervised", "-dim").stderr.startswith(
            "-dim is missing an argument\n\n"))
        self.assertTrue(self.run_cli("supervised", "-loss", "bad").stderr.startswith(
            "Unknown loss: bad\n\n"))

    def test_missing_and_invalid_models(self):
        result = self.run_cli("print-word-vectors", "missing.bin")
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("missing.bin cannot be opened for loading!", result.stderr)
        invalid = self.directory / "invalid.bin"
        invalid.write_text("not a model")
        result = self.run_cli("dump", invalid, "args")
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("has wrong file format!", result.stderr)

    def test_dictionary_and_saved_arguments(self):
        model = self.train("-epoch", 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("dump", model, "dict").stdout,
                         "5\n</s> 2 word\nx 1 word\ny 1 word\n"
                         "__label__a 1 label\n__label__b 1 label\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("dump", model, "args").stdout,
                         "dim 2\nws 5\nepoch 0\nminCount 1\nneg 5\n"
                         "wordNgrams 2\nloss softmax\nmodel sup\nbucket 100\n"
                         "minn 0\nmaxn 0\nlrUpdateRate 100\nt 0.0001\n")
        self.assertEqual(struct.unpack("<ii", model.read_bytes()[:8]), (793712314, 12))
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("dump", model, "output").stdout, "2 2\n0 0\n0 0\n")

    def test_one_epoch_numerical_update(self):
        model = self.train("-epoch", 1, "-lrUpdateRate", 0, "-saveOutput")
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("dump", model, "output").stdout,
                         "2 2\n-0.0106571 0.00105498\n0.0106571 -0.00105498\n")
        self.assertTrue(self.model.with_suffix(".output").exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("print-word-vectors", model, text="unknown\n").stdout,
                         "unknown 0 0 \n")

    def test_prediction_ties_and_thresholds(self):
        model = self.train("-epoch", 0)
        result = self.run_cli("predict-prob", model, "-", 2, text="x\n\ny\n")
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,
                         "__label__b 0.50001 __label__a 0.50001\n" * 3)
        result = self.run_cli("predict-prob", model, "-", 2, 0.500005, text="x\n")
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "\n")
        result = self.run_cli("predict", model, "-", 0, text="x\n")
        self.assertIn("k needs to be 1 or higher!", result.stderr)

    def test_evaluation_format(self):
        model = self.train("-epoch", 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("test", model, self.corpus, 2).stdout,
                         "N\t2\nP@2\t0.5\nR@2\t1\n")
        result = self.run_cli("test-label", model, self.corpus, 2)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,
                         "F1-Score : 0.666667  Precision : 0.500000  Recall : 1.000000   __label__a\n"
                         "F1-Score : 0.666667  Precision : 0.500000  Recall : 1.000000   __label__b\n"
                         "N\t2\nP@2\t0.500\nR@2\t1.000\n")

        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli("test", model, "-", text=self.corpus.read_text()).stdout,

        self.corpus.write_text("__label__a x\n__label__b y\n__label__c z\n__label__d q\n")
        for loss in ("softmax", "hs", "ns", "ova"):
            with self.subTest(loss=loss):

                result = self.run_cli("predict", model, "-", text="x\ny\nz\nq\n")
                self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "__label__a\n__label__b\n__label__c\n__label__d\n")

        model = self.train("-minCount", 1, "-dim", 3, "-epoch", 0,
                           command="skipgram")
        result = self.run_cli("print-word-vectors", model, text="one\n")
